comparison: Both address the main novelty claim (C84, C126, C132). OpenEval finds the conclusions SUPPORTED and appropriately qualified, while peer reviewers strongly challenge novelty, stating VH is 'similar to distractor heterogeneity' and 'an unnecessary term'. Major disagreement on whether VH represents a genuinely novel concept.

Both evaluate the core behavioral correlations (C33, C34, C64, C65). OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED with appropriate statistics and theoretical motivation. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising fundamental concerns about circularity from center-fitting and noting the positive correlation 'reflects the classic target-distractor similarity effect' rather than novelty.

Both address VH neural localization claims (C47, C48, C71, C72, C107, C109). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate searchlight analysis and cross-validation. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED due to poor overlap between VH regions across experiments, stating 'VHsymmetry and VHdetection are nearly non-overlapping' and rejecting the claim of discovering a new area.

Both discuss model limitations and overlap in VH values (C35, C36, C66, C67, C90). OpenEval finds the acknowledgment of limitations SUPPORTED and reasonable. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting the overlap as problematic for the theory and that 'acknowledgement of flaws does not argue in favor of publication.'

Both evaluate validation analyses (C37, C38, C39, C163, C164). OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED as rigorous controls addressing circularity and overfitting. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, dismissing these efforts as insufficient, stating 'center-fitting should not be done in the first place' and that DNN validation 'cannot provide stronger evidence.'

Both address behavioral paradigm quality (C24, C25, C29, C30, C31, C58, C59, C61, C62). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate sample size and reliability. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, acknowledging 'carefully designed experiments' and 'scientific rigor' without challenging basic data quality.

Both evaluate LO's role in encoding perceptual dissimilarities (C53, C54, C55, C75, C77). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED and consistent with prior literature. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, noting 'solid evidence for the involvement of higher-order visual cortex' and not disputing this aspect.

Both address cross-task generalization claims (C43, C79, C80). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to missing appendix data but finds the claim plausible. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, rejecting the interpretation of a common mechanism and questioning the assumption that 'all of these tasks must have a common explanation.'

Both discuss dissociation between VH activity and RT-related activations (C50, C51, C52, C73, C74). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as evidence VH encodes something distinct from task difficulty. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, not specifically challenging these dissociations.

Both address VH as intrinsic image property and context-independence (C44, C45, C100, C101, C127, C128). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to missing appendix data but notes theoretical motivation. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, challenging that VH was 'calculated on the basis of reaction times instead' of image properties directly.
OpenEval finds the summary conclusion (C42) SUPPORTED by combined behavioral and validation evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this summary claim.
OpenEval rates results from Appendix 4 (C43) as UNCERTAIN due to missing data. Peer reviewers address C43 in R8 regarding cross-task mechanisms but not specifically the appendix validation.
OpenEval rates Appendix 6 results on averaging assumption (C56) as UNCERTAIN due to missing data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval finds Experiment 3 design and symmetry spacing results (C57-C60) SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers address related behavioral data quality in R6 but not these specific claims.

OpenEval finds symmetry detection correlations (C61-C65) SUPPORTED despite being weaker than Experiment 2. Peer reviewers address C64-C65 in R2 regarding circularity concerns but not the full result set.
OpenEval finds acknowledgment of VH limitations for symmetry (C66-C68) SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers address C66-C67 in R4 as problematic but not as a standalone evaluation.
OpenEval finds summary conclusions about unified principle (C69-C70) SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this summary.
OpenEval finds RSA results showing LO encodes perceptual space while VH encodes distance-to-center (C75-C78) SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers address C75, C77 in R7 but not the full architectural claim.
OpenEval rates categorization reanalysis (C81-C83) as UNCERTAIN due to missing Appendix 10. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval finds interpretation of target-absent slopes via VH (C87-C90) SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers address C90 in R4 regarding limitations but not the slope interpretation.
OpenEval rates same-different task interpretation (C91-C93) as UNCERTAIN due to missing appendix. Peer reviewers address related claims in R8 but not these specific claims.
OpenEval finds contrast with traditional symmetry models (C94-C97) SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval rates distinction between VH and average distance (C98-C101) as UNCERTAIN due to missing appendices. Peer reviewers address C100-C101 in R10 but not the full distinction claim.
OpenEval finds neuroimaging summary and norm-based encoding discussion (C107-C110) SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers address C107, C109 in R3 regarding localization but not the norm-based interpretation.
OpenEval finds animate/inanimate differences explanation via VH (C117-C121) SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval finds explanation of prior literature findings (C122-C123) SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval rates operational definition of VH (C126-C128) as UNCERTAIN due to missing appendix on context-independence. Peer reviewers address C126, C128 in R1 and R10 but not as operational definition evaluation.
OpenEval finds main conclusions (C132-C134) SUPPORTED and appropriately qualified. Peer reviewers address C132 in R1 regarding novelty but not the full conclusion set.
OpenEval finds model specification and validation (C163-C166) SUPPORTED with appropriate rigor. Peer reviewers address C163-C164 in R5 regarding validation but not model parsimony.
